findings.F1: The bars starting at 21:00 and 22:00 UTC gain +0.049 % per hour on average, against +0.003 % in every other hour (Welch t 10.8, about 69 000 bars). The gain is positive on every weekday (t 2.0 to 7.7) and in 7 of 8 years (t 2.3 to 11.3; 2022 is the exception at t −4.6). It is positive in all 19 coins and largest in the more volatile ones (NEAR +0.101 %, DOGE +0.087 %, TRX +0.016 %).
findings.F2: Take each coin's 48-hour return up to Friday 00:00 UTC, standardised by its usual 48-hour move. That return is followed by a move the same way over Friday and Saturday: slope +0.073, t 5.5, 4 204 cases. After a rise, the unusual move is +0.89 % (t 5.6). The top quintile ends +0.22 of a usual move above drift, against +0.004 for the bottom quintile. The slope is positive in 6 of 8 years (t +4.0 in 2018, +4.0 in 2025).
findings.F3: In the tested Monday cases (744 with a full 96-hour path), the reversal falls on Tuesday. The Monday 00:00 to Tuesday 00:00 return is +0.11 % (t 0.45), the Tuesday return is −0.62 % (t −2.74), and Wednesday–Thursday gives +0.77 % back (t 1.38).
findings.F4: The weekend reversal holds only in the high-volatility regime: the slope of the Monday–Tuesday move on the weekend move is −0.125 (t −4.3, 1 666 cases), and the top quintile of weekend rises is followed by −1.38 % unusual. In calm regimes the slope is +0.066 (t 2.25, 2 499 cases), and a weekend fall is followed by a further unusual −0.68 % (t −3.43).
findings.F5: Early-week reversal is not specific to the weekend. The 48-hour returns ending Tuesday 00:00 and Wednesday 00:00 are reversed over the next 48 hours about as strongly as the weekend move (slopes −0.063 t −3.8 and −0.058 t −3.8, against −0.056 t −2.8 for Monday).
findings.F6: The book does not hold the idea's 48 hours. Of 1 586 short trades, all entered at Sunday 23:00 UTC, only 623 last 47–49 hours, and those earn +0.80 % gross. The 738 trades shorter than 47 hours lose −1.98 % gross, and the 182 trades longer than 200 hours lose −2.69 %. Overall the trades lose −1.12 % gross and −1.22 % net, while the idea's total move per case is +0.84 %.

ideas.idea: A coin's 48-hour return up to Friday 00:00 UTC carries on over Friday and Saturday: the larger its rise over Wednesday and Thursday, the larger its further rise over the next 2 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader would lean with a midweek rise into the weekend rather than fade it, and refuse a short against a strong Wednesday–Thursday rise.
ideas.name: midweek rise carries into weekend

ideas.idea: A coin's price rises over the two hours from 21:00 to 23:00 UTC each day, by more the higher the coin's volatility over its last 30 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader would place buys before 21:00 UTC rather than after 23:00 UTC, and avoid selling into those two hours.
ideas.name: late-evening UTC drift up

ideas.idea: While a coin's 30-day hourly volatility is high against its last 6 months, a rise from Saturday 00:00 to Monday 00:00 UTC is followed by a fall over Tuesday (Tuesday 00:00 to Wednesday 00:00 UTC): the larger the weekend gain, the larger the Tuesday fall.
ideas.consequence: A trader would fade a turbulent-week weekend rise on Tuesday only, sparing the cost of carrying it through a flat Monday.
ideas.name: turbulent weekend rise, Tuesday fall

ideas.idea: While a coin's 30-day hourly volatility is low against its last 6 months, a fall from Saturday 00:00 to Monday 00:00 UTC is followed by a further fall over Monday and Tuesday: the larger the weekend fall, the larger the further fall.
ideas.consequence: A trader would not buy a weekend dip in calm weeks and would treat it as a reason to stay short over the next 2 days.
ideas.name: calm weekend fall continues
